findings.summary: The criterion 4 fixture conflicts with the plan's own studies-only guard, so the test may fail with the correct code, or pass only by accident
findings.evidence: The plan uses `fx.athena(rated_scenario().script())`. rated_scenario's reading lists only studies/demo/pin.json, claims.json and intro.json as deliverables (crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs:6062-6067). After a read, plan_entry takes `touches` from those deliverables. Plan step 3 makes `is_fix_request` return false when every touched path is under `studies/`. The dependents entry says the criterion 4 test uses 'an unread steward request that the pass reads (the same shape as real_steps_read_an_unread_but_specifiable_request_once_and_then_run_it)'. After that read (drain.rs:2276-2283), `mark_fixes` sees studies-only touches and clears the flag. The feature request is then dispatched first and the test fails even though the code is right. Without the read, the re-read path that the dependents entry claims the test covers is never exercised. Fix: Give the criterion 4 steward request bullets and a `crates/` path, so it is planned from its own words without a read. Add a second case that does go through the read pass with a reader scenario whose deliverables are under `crates/`, and assert that the flag survives the re-read. State both in the demonstration, and remove the claim that one test covers both paths.

findings.summary: The approved-decision link in records_fix_inputs can never produce a fix
findings.evidence: Only proposals can be decided: work_decisions::find_open refuses any kind other than Proposal (crates/athena-core/src/work_decisions.rs:107-109). The plan rules that a Proposal is never a fix. An approved work item is therefore always a Proposal and is never flagged. A unit test of this link would have to build an approved BlindSpot or RepeatedFailure item, which production cannot create. Fix: Drop the approved-decision branch, or keep it with a comment that it is unreachable today. Do not cite a unit test of an impossible state as coverage.
findings.location: Plan step 5 (records_fix_inputs); Risks, first bullet ('a unit test covers the approved-decision link')

findings.summary: The build_capped case in criterion 2 contradicts the dependents note, and the cap-slot effect is not tested
findings.evidence: The dependents note says a fix entry 'keeps a cap slot ahead of feature entries, which is the intended effect'. Cap slots go to entries in uncapped plan order (plan.rs:811-818, 847-865), so a newer high fix entry would now push an older high feature entry down to normal. Demonstration (e) instead says the fix entry 'does not take a high slot it would not otherwise hold'. For a normal fix entry that holds whatever the code does, so it shows nothing. Fix: Choose the intended behavior. Then test that a high fix entry takes the single high slot and demotes an older high feature entry (person-set entries excepted), or make it not do so. Record the choice in D181, because it affects which item the caps demote.

findings.summary: The plan does not measure how many of the 52 starved steward requests the narrower classification flags
findings.evidence: validate_item maps every steward item that is not RepeatedFailure to WorkItemKind::Proposal (crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs:1045-1048), and a briefed item always becomes a Proposal (steward.rs:723-727). Under the plan, any steward request that fixes Athena code but was filed as a Proposal keeps its age place. The accepted reading also allowed a key or title route for root-cause fixes, which the plan drops. The reading's stated goal ('the steward's filed requests stop starving') may therefore be only partly met. The records are not in the snapshot, so the split by kind is unknown. Fix: In D181 and the changelog, say that only steward BlindSpot and RepeatedFailure items are ranked as fixes, that this departs from the reading's key and title route, and that the share of the 52 requests this covers was not measured. Name the typed marker a later change would add for steward Proposals that fix Athena.

findings.summary: Two more prose statements of the order are not updated
findings.evidence: README.md:145-148 says 'a higher rung goes first, an item that depends on another comes after it, and age only breaks ties'. docs/design/roles-and-ladder.md:73-74 says 'a wave is ordered by rung (top first), then age'. The plan cites D156 to justify updating main.rs and drain.rs docs, but leaves these two order statements out. Fix: Add a one-line update to README.md and roles-and-ladder.md saying that, inside a priority, requests that fix Athena itself come first. If the scope should stay narrow, name them in D181 as known stale text.

findings.summary: The studies-only guard reads a signal that changes after reading, so the flag can flip
findings.evidence: `entry.touches` comes from path-like words in the request before it is read, and from the reading's deliverables after (topics.rs plan_entry; drain.rs:2282-2283). The same work item can be flagged before a read and not after, or the other way round. Steward website and study requests are already excluded by kind Proposal (steward.rs:1045-1048), so the guard only acts on BlindSpot and RepeatedFailure items. Fix: Base the content guard on a stable field: the work item's `source` path, or the request text's own paths. Or drop it and rely on the kind rule, and say so in D181.

summary: The core design is sound and fixes the fault where it starts. The plan changes the one sort inside the best-priority ready set in Plan::build_with (plan.rs:780-783), and both `athena plan` and `athena drain` reach that sort through drain::plan → steps.queue() → RealSteps::entry_of (drain.rs:3448-3459, 4527-4530). So priority and dependencies cannot be overridden. Classifying through typed records (work-item kind, Hestia's cause links and the gate line) is defensible. The owner's list maps onto the kinds the steward emits (BlindSpot, RepeatedFailure; steward.rs:1045-1048) and the requests Hestia generates (root_cause_request, gate_request). One demonstration has a real defect, so the verdict is revise. The criterion 4 drain test uses the rated_scenario reader, whose reading lists only studies/demo/ deliverables (tests/drain.rs:6062-6067). The plan's own studies-only guard would then clear the fix flag on the steward blind-spot request as soon as it is read, and the dependents section says the test goes through exactly that read path. The minor findings: the approved-decision link can never produce a fix; the build_capped case contradicts the dependents note; the README and the roles-and-ladder doc still describe the old order; and the plan does not say how many of the 52 starved requests the narrower classification will actually reach.
